You're in findings-verification mode, not scoring mode. Reviewing PR #74 on zimmermann-pwa (branch `feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches`, base `269d5d40149b9947111dd87e78d37b92fccd4c99`, head `54e924ffddabef17aeabb983873c60855dd06aac` = current HEAD, no checkout needed — read the working tree as-is or `git diff` the range yourself).

For each finding below: does it survive scrutiny? Reproduce it from source or say you could not. Return CONFIRMED (reproduced from source), PLAUSIBLE (consistent with what you read, decisive evidence missing — say exactly what would settle it), or UNSUPPORTED (the citation doesn't support the claim — say what's actually true). Where a finding's conclusion is broader than its search supports, downgrade it and say so.

## Findings to verify

**F1 — Lint regression.** Claim: `npm run lint` on HEAD produces 2 more errors than on BASE, both prettier-formatting errors in PR-added files: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:86` and `.../zimmColourSwatch/index.test.tsx:119`. I measured this myself by running the gate on both SHAs (base=4 errors/16 warnings, head=6 errors/16 warnings, same 16 warnings just line-shifted). You can re-run `npm run lint` on HEAD only to confirm those 2 specific errors still exist at those locations — no need to reconstruct BASE.

**F2 — Stale/self-contradictory comment.** File `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`, around lines 159-168. Claim: the comment immediately above the `pageButton._disabled` object says "No confirmed Figma spec for a disabled visual treatment on this control... only the cursor affordance is set here, which is a UX keyword, not a design token" — but the `_disabled` object right below it sets BOTH `cursor: 'not-allowed'` AND `color: 'var(--zimm-color-icon-disabled)'`, which IS a real visual treatment via a real design token, directly contradicting the comment. Read the actual lines and confirm or refute.

**F3 — Over-delivery: unused `href`-absent branch.** Files `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx` (the `href?: string` prop and the `if (href) {...} return <chakra.span>...` branch) and `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx`. Claim: this PR's only real wiring (`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`, the `renderVariationAttribute` prop passed to the main uncontrolled `<ProductView>`) always supplies a real `href` for every colour value — `href: null`/undefined only occurs via SFCC's controlled-mode variation-attributes path (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-variation-attributes.js`, the `isControlled`/`controlledVariationValues` branch), which this PR never wires `renderVariationAttribute` into (not `product-view-modal`, not `bonus-product-view-modal`). So the href-absent branch, its dedicated prop, several unit tests, and a whole Storybook story currently have no live caller anywhere in this PR's actual scope. Verify by tracing: does `product-detail/index.tsx` ever render `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`/pass `renderVariationAttribute` anywhere other than the one call site on the main product `<ProductView>`? Does that hook's controlled-mode branch really only trigger from a different component this PR doesn't touch?

**F4 — Missing `_hover` state, codebase-convention violation.** Files `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` and `.../zimmColourSwatchGroup/zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`. Claim: neither of this PR's two new interactive recipes (`swatch` part, an anchor/span; `pageButton` part, a button) defines a `_hover` block, while every other interactive recipe already in `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` — check `zimmNavItem/zimmNavItem.css.ts`, `zimmTextInput/zimmTextInput.css.ts`, `zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts` — does define one. I independently checked Figma myself (file `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`, node `40000307:13823` "pdp/product-colour-picker" and node `40003328:115591` "Pagination") and confirmed there is genuinely no Hover-state variant defined anywhere in this component set (only Unselected/Selected/Focus states exist) — so this is a codebase-convention question, not a missed Figma spec. Just verify the code-side claim: do the 3 cited sibling files really all define `_hover`, and do the 2 new files really define none?

**F5 — Missing test file for `product-view/index.tsx`.** Claim: `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` gained real new branching logic in this PR (the `renderVariationAttribute?.(attr) ?? renderDefaultVariationAttribute(attr)` fallback) but has no `index.test.ts`/`index.test.tsx` anywhere in its folder, on either base or head. Verify the file genuinely doesn't exist (not just "didn't show up in a grep").

**F6 — Silent loss of unorderable/out-of-stock colour treatment.** Claim: `v.orderable` (a real field on the SFCC variation value shape) is never forwarded from `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` into `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s `values` mapping, and `ZimmColourSwatchValue`'s type has no such field at all — so an unorderable-but-image-populated colour now renders identically to an orderable one, with no comment anywhere acknowledging this narrowing (contrast with the `pageButton._disabled` block, which does have an explicit comment about its own unspecified state). Verify: grep for `orderable` in `product-detail/index.tsx` and in the `zimmColourSwatchGroup`/`zimmColourSwatch` type definitions — is it really absent end to end?

**F7 — `href` type should include `null`.** Claim: `href?: string` is declared in both `zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx` and `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx`, but the real hook this data traces back to (`use-variation-attributes.js`) returns `href: null` (not `undefined`) in its controlled-mode branch — a type-accuracy gap, not a functional bug (`if (href)` treats both the same). Verify the hook really returns `null` specifically, not `undefined`, in that branch.

**F8 — Pagination test-suite doesn't test the actual click-triggered transition.** File `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.test.tsx`. Claim: existing tests either check a fresh mount already on the correct/wrong page, or click prev/next and assert only on rendered `width`/item-count — none clicks a pagination button and then asserts on `tabindex`/`aria-checked` of the resulting swatches. This means nothing in the shipped suite would catch a regression of the WCAG roving-tabindex-after-paging fix if it were reintroduced. Verify by reading the actual test file's assertions after each `userEvent.click` on a pagination button.

**F9 — Single-frame stale-pagination flash on cross-product navigation (already labeled PLAUSIBLE by its source, not CONFIRMED).** Claim: because no component in the tree keys `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`/`ProductView` by product identity, and `pageStart` state persists across a prop-driven re-render (only corrected by a `useEffect` on the next tick), navigating from one paginated product to a different paginated product could in principle paint one stale frame before self-correcting. The original source couldn't construct a jsdom repro (effects flush synchronously in RTL) and says so explicitly. Don't try to force a repro either — just assess whether the reasoning about the component tree (no remount, effect-based correction) holds up from reading the actual code, and state plainly that this remains unconfirmed by execution either way.

## What's already settled — don't re-litigate

- All 5 real Jira ACs (single-colour label-only, swatch-per-populated-colour, selected-indication, URL-update-without-reload, unpopulated-image-filtered) are independently confirmed implemented correctly by two separate passes already (file:line evidence exists) — not in question.
- Every colour/spacing/typography token match against live Figma (bottom-border colour/width, background colour, focus-ring colour/width/offset, `caption` textStyle, disabled-chevron colour) was verified directly against the Figma file by a human-directed pass, including live computed-style verification in a running Storybook via real keyboard `Tab` navigation. Not in question.
- The Tier 1 foundation-file edit (`colour.ts`/`zimmTokens.ts`) was independently re-verified as genuinely authorized (`gh api` confirms the PR author is both a `tier-1-approvers` member and repo admin) by two separate checks already. Not in question — don't re-check GitHub team membership.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` are clean/unchanged between base and head — not in question.
- `npm run test` (vitest) is 433/433 passing on head, no regressions — not in question.

Report back with each finding's ID, verdict (CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE/UNSUPPORTED), and one line of evidence or the specific gap in evidence.

5	 * variation's product photo. Two parts: `swatch` is the outer clickable box (geometry,

7	 * background-image fill — the URL itself cannot live here, see the component's own comment on

13	 */
14	export const ZimmColourSwatch = {
15	  parts: ['swatch', 'image'],
16	
17	  baseStyle: ({ selected }: { selected?: boolean }): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
18	    swatch: {
19	      display: 'inline-block',
20	      cursor: 'pointer',
21	      // Figma's Rectangle width (48px). Height (72px) has no direct token — the named scale has
22	      // nothing between 64px and 140px — so it's expressed as an aspect ratio on the width
23	      // instead. 2:3, not the incidentally different ratio Figma's raw code-gen attached to the
24	      // placeholder product photo pasted into that frame instance: the Selected-state node
25	      // carries its own dev annotation reading "Image aspect ratio - 2:3", which is the number
26	      // to trust here.
27	      width: 'var(--zimm-scale-1200)',
28	      aspectRatio: '2 / 3',
29	      // Identical across Unselected/Selected/Focus — ivory[200] / background['02'] in
30	      // theme/foundation/colour.ts.
31	      backgroundColor: 'var(--zimm-color-bg-02)',
32	      // Selected: a bottom-only border — the raw Figma export is unambiguous, a `border-b`
33	      // utility rather than a full box border. Colour is grey[900] / border.focus, the only
34	      // alias-tier value that resolves to it (border.default and border.secondary are both
35	      // light greys and never appear anywhere in this design).
36	      ...(selected
37	        ? {
38	            borderBottomWidth: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default)',
39	            borderBottomStyle: 'solid',
40	            borderBottomColor: 'var(--zimm-color-border-focus)',
41	          }
42	        : {}),
43	      // Focus: Figma draws this as the Selected baseline plus a ring at slightly asymmetric
44	      // per-side offsets, same colour. Not replicated literally — there is no other precedent
45	      // anywhere in this codebase for a non-uniform ring, and the asymmetry reads as that one
46	      // frame instance's export noise rather than a deliberate design decision. Mirrors
47	      // zimmNavItem.css.ts's own focus-ring block instead: a uniform `outline` + `outlineOffset`
48	      // pair, applied independently of `selected` above — a swatch can be focused without being
49	      // selected, and selected without being focused. `--zimm-focus-ring` already composites the
50	      // same border-width/colour pair used above; `--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default` matches
51	      // three of Figma's four side offsets.
52	      //
53	      // `position: relative` + `zIndex: 1`, scoped to this focus-visible state only: the parent
54	      // `swatches` row (zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts) is `gap: 0`, so adjacent swatches sit
55	      // flush. `outlineOffset` is positive, so the ring paints *outside* this swatch's own
56	      // border box — and with zero gap, that outward ring overlaps the very next swatch's own
57	      // box. Both swatches are plain in-flow flex items (`position: static`, `z-index: auto`),
58	      // so painting follows tree order: the later sibling paints its opaque background on top
59	      // of the earlier swatch's ring wherever the two overlap, hiding exactly the shared
60	      // (right-hand) edge — confirmed in a real Chromium render, before this fix, via
61	      // `getBoundingClientRect`/`elementFromPoint` and a screenshot: the right edge and the
62	      // right-hand slivers of the top/bottom edges were missing for every swatch with a
63	      // right-hand sibling, while the last swatch in a row (nothing to its right) rendered a
64	      // complete rectangle. `zIndex` lifts this swatch into a later, higher paint layer so its
65	      // ring is no longer covered; `position: relative` is what makes `zIndex` apply here at
66	      // all for a *general* in-flow, non-positioned element — without it `z-index` is ignored
67	      // per spec. (A `swatch` specifically is also a direct flex item of `swatches`, and the
68	      // Flexbox spec carves out flex items as one exception where `z-index` alone establishes
69	      // a stacking context even while `position` stays `static` — confirmed empirically here
70	      // too, `z-index` alone did already fix this swatch's own outline. `position: relative` is
71	      // kept anyway: it costs nothing — no `top`/`left`/etc. offset is set, so it does not move
72	      // the box — and it keeps this rule correct even if `swatch` is ever composed inside a
73	      // non-flex parent, rather than depending on a layout detail owned by a sibling file.)
74	      // Neither property is set outside `_focusVisible`, so normal (unfocused) stacking is
75	      // completely unaffected.
76	      _focusVisible: {

78	        zIndex: 1,

## Findings verification — PR #74 (`feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches`)

**F1 — Lint regression. CONFIRMED.**
Ran `npm run lint` on HEAD as instructed (no BASE reconstruction needed). Output: `✖ 22 problems (6 errors, 16 warnings)` — matches the claimed head count exactly. Two of the six errors are exactly where claimed:
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:86:17` (`prettier/prettier`) and `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.test.tsx:119:30` (`prettier/prettier`).

**F2 — Stale/self-contradictory comment. CONFIRMED.**
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts:159-168`. The comment states "only the cursor affordance is set here, which is a UX keyword, not a design token," but the `_disabled` block immediately below sets both `cursor: 'not-allowed'` **and** `color: 'var(--zimm-color-icon-disabled)'` — a real `--zimm-*` token. Consistent with the `color` line being a later addition (commit `0aff491`, "disabled chevron colour") that the comment above it was never updated for.

**F3 — Over-delivery: unused `href`-absent branch. CONFIRMED.**
Traced the full chain: `product-detail/index.tsx` has exactly one `renderVariationAttribute` call site (line 913, on the single non-set/bundle `<ProductView>` at line 901), which never passes `controlledVariationValues` (zero grep matches in the file) and always maps `href: v.href`. The other two `<ProductView>` instances (lines 811, 837 — set/bundle children) never pass `renderVariationAttribute` at all. `use-variation-attributes.js:151-153` confirms `href` is only ever null when `controlledVariationValues !== null`. Neither `product-view-modal/` nor `bonus-product-view-modal/` is overridden anywhere in this repo (`ls` confirms no such directories under `overrides/app/components/`), and the base (node_modules) versions of both never reference `renderVariationAttribute` — so even via the ccExtensibility redirect, that path can't reach `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`. Repo-wide grep confirms the only non-test/non-story importers of the two new components are `theme/components/index.ts` (registration) and `product-detail/index.tsx` (the one covered call site). The href-absent branch has 5 dedicated tests (`zimmColourSwatch/index.test.tsx:72,78,83,88,93`) and its own story (`WithoutLink`, `index.stories.tsx:63`).

**F4 — Missing `_hover` state. CONFIRMED.**
`grep` confirms zero `_hover` occurrences in `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` (only `_focusVisible`, line 76) and `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts` (only `_disabled`/`_focusVisible`, lines 165/171). All three cited siblings define `_hover`: `zimmNavItem.css.ts:46`, `zimmTextInput.css.ts:101`, `zimmButton.css.ts:46,68,93,124,155,179`.

**F5 — Missing test file for `product-view/index.tsx`. CONFIRMED.**
`find` on the folder returns only `index.tsx`, on both HEAD and the base commit (`git ls-tree <base-sha> -- overrides/app/components/product-view/`). `git log --follow` over the folder's entire history shows no test file has ever existed there. Repo-wide grep confirms no test file imports `product-view`, directly or indirectly.

**F6 — Silent loss of unorderable/out-of-stock treatment. PLAUSIBLE (downgraded from what would otherwise be CONFIRMED — the "no comment anywhere" clause overstates the record).**
The behavioural core is fully reproduced: `orderable` is absent from `product-detail/index.tsx`'s mapping (zero matches), absent from `ZimmColourSwatchValue`/`ZimmColourSwatchGroupProps` entirely, and the base `product-view/index.tsx`'s own `renderDefaultVariationAttribute` *does* use it (`disabled={!orderable}`, ~line 736) — confirming this is a real, precedented behaviour the new colour path diverges from. However, "no comment anywhere acknowledging this narrowing" is not accurate: `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:47-49` ("...regardless of any stock/orderability field it might otherwise carry") and `:78-80` ("Content-population, not stock/orderability — the filter keys on `imageUrl` alone"), plus a dedicated test (`index.test.tsx:100-107`), explicitly name and address the orderable/stock concept in-code. What's true: those comments justify the *filter* decision, not the specific "renders with no disabled affordance" consequence — so the omission is real and evidently deliberate, just not literally uncommented.

**F7 — `href` type should include `null`. CONFIRMED.**
`use-variation-attributes.js:151-153`: `href: isControlled ? null : buildVariantValueHref({...})` — an explicit `null`, not `undefined`, in the controlled-mode branch.

**F8 — Pagination suite doesn't test the click-triggered transition. CONFIRMED.**
Read every test in `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.test.tsx`: exactly one (`lines 170-217`) clicks a pagination button, and its post-click assertions are only radio count and CSS `width` — no `tabindex`/`aria-checked` check anywhere after a click in the whole file. I additionally checked `index.stories.tsx`'s `Paginated` story (the test file's own docblock delegates "pagination-window interaction" to it) — its `play` (lines 172-195) clicks next/previous twice but only asserts radio count, one named radio's absence, and button-disabled state; its single post-click `aria-checked` assertion re-checks the already-selected element, never the "which swatch becomes the new tab stop" case the WCAG fix addresses. The gap holds across the entire shipped suite, not just the cited file.
